test_title: PYST 14: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 13 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In April 2025, IN-SPACe launched an initiative inviting private firms to develop modular satellite platforms to host multiple payloads, aiming to reduce reliance on foreign satellite infrastructure. What is this initiative called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Satellite Bus as a Service (SBaaS)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **April 2025**, **IN-SPACe** (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Center) launched an initiative to invite private firms to participate in the development of **modular satellite platforms**. This is aimed at enabling **multi-payload hosting** to reduce dependency on foreign satellite infrastructure. *This statement is correct.*
 
• The initiative was named **"Satellite Bus as a Service" (SBaaS)**. It focuses on providing **modular and scalable satellite buses** to host multiple payloads, allowing private companies to utilize the platform for commercial and scientific purposes. *Hence, the name of the initiative is correct.*
 
• The purpose of the SBaaS initiative is to **reduce costs** and **timeframes** for satellite deployment by creating a **standardized platform**. This benefits private space companies by offering a plug-and-play satellite bus solution. *Hence, the initiative aligns with its goals.*
 
• It also seeks to **enhance the competitiveness of Indian private space firms** on the global stage by providing **indigenous satellite solutions**. This supports the broader vision of **"Atmanirbhar Bharat" (Self-reliant India)** in the space sector. *This is a correct observation.*
 
• The **SBaaS initiative** is a collaborative effort between IN-SPACe, private firms, and startups to **boost innovation** and **promote the commercialization of space technologies**. *Hence, it is a correct statement.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IN-SPACe:**

 
 
• **IN-SPACe** was established in **2020** as an autonomous body under the **Department of Space (DoS)** to promote and regulate the participation of **non-governmental entities (NGEs)** in the space sector.
 
• It facilitates private firms in **developing, testing, and launching space technologies** and ensures collaboration with ISRO for technical and infrastructural support.
 
 
 
• **Satellite Bus:**
 
 
• A **satellite bus** is the core framework of a satellite that includes components such as **power systems, thermal control, and propulsion systems**. It serves as a base structure to host various payloads.
 
• The **modular satellite buses** reduce the design complexity and allow multiple organizations to use a single platform for launching their payloads.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of SBaaS:**
 
 
• **Cost Efficiency**: Reduces costs associated with designing and building custom satellite buses for individual payloads.
 
• **Time-Saving**: Decreases the time required for satellite development and deployment.
 
• **Commercialization**: Encourages private players to invest in space technology by providing ready-to-use solutions.
 
• **Global Competitiveness**: Enhances India's position in the **global satellite market** by offering indigenous solutions.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Space Initiatives:**
 
 
• **PSLV-C53 Mission**: A dedicated commercial satellite launch mission by ISRO.
 
• **Indian Space Association (ISpA)**: Established to facilitate collaboration between the government and private players in the space sector.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The SBaaS initiative is part of India's broader effort to **develop indigenous space technology** and reduce reliance on foreign infrastructure.
 
• The program encourages the **participation of startups**, providing them with opportunities to test and deploy their technologies.
 
• It aligns with the **global trend of commercializing the space industry**, promoting innovation, and ensuring **sustainable and cost-effective space missions**.
 
• By inviting private firms, India aims to strengthen its **space ecosystem** and increase its contribution to the **global satellite market**, which is projected to grow significantly in the coming years.
